source_en:
In the hunt for Aegoroth, Eye of the Abyss, I grow closer. A resident from the Inn claims to have come across a most peculiar people. Just three days journey from here. To hear him say it, during his travels in the Armaea Hills he came across a small wooden structure, what he thought was a church. Upon closer inspection, he found the building empty. 

Being a storm coming, he decided to shelter for the night. It must have been the lightning that saved him--for he awoke startled by the flash and in that wisp of light, he found men standing all around him, spread about in a fanning circle, all watching him sleep, all with empty hollows where there should be eyes.

Just like that, the light passed and he was left in the dark. And when the next flash came-they were gone. It is said that devout followers relinquish their eyes to Aegoroth for just a glimpse of his flesh. Lunacy. Fanatics. Obviously. But still, a fantastic opportunity for a firsthand interview! They must know more about the lost legends of this fabled creature than any.  

I shall begin my journey tomorrow.

source_en:
The first question one must ask when inquiring on the true inception point of knowledge, is 
the question of dreams. Where do they come from? Are they merely our internal 
hallucinations by sleep? Or is it a thread dripping through the ether, providing knowledge 
from the other side? From some one or some thing on the other side of the veil. 
I have been with the Aegorothians for a fortnight and they have me questioning my 
preconceptions.  
Lunatics, maybe. But these men and women willingly gave their eyes to their god. Plucked 
one by one as grapes for the Eye of the Abyss. And not a single one claims that they cannot 
see. 
They say it started with dreams. Dreams of knowledge. Dreams of sight. In these dreams, 
they see impossible things and eventually, Aegoroth himself. They describe large, 
magnificent wings and many, many eyes. Blue irises. And brown. Every kind. 
Could it be that all this time true knowledge came from the other side traveling through our 
dreams. Forbidden knowledge from a gracious god.  
And if it is true, I wonder, will he visit me?

I must now take my leave of Gildenarch. When the Archspire finds Renault’s smoldering corpse, I will most certainly be hanged.

I was, however, successful. Just as before, Renault successfully completed the ritual, but Apothos was none too pleased. I did not inform Renault that I would try to bind the Angel once it had taken over him; I knew he wouldn’t have agreed, but I was too close to let anything get in my way. Too many have died for me to get answers already.

Once I bound the Angel, I commanded Apothos to tell me why the Divine is silent. 

Aothos Spoke:

“Afflicted by the malady of eternity

What is taken must one day be returned.

In time, the Throne will Coil its Lord 

And the Serpent will reawaken.”

They do not serve the Divine. They serve the Throne itself. This faith-shattering revelation must not be lost. What we are told is a lie; the Divine hasn’t turned his back on us for our sins… he is dying.. Does The Holy Lineage know this?

source_en:
A theory so bizarre it may at least hold a glimmer of truth. Allegedly, one of the Archspire’s Scribes was detained for suggesting a shared lineage between the Angels and the Demons. Now such a claim deserves little more than mockery and wouldn’t have aroused a bit of suspicion, but why punish him over mere, albeit absurd, speculation? 

Silencing a man does more to draw attention than his own words…


The Scribe’s disciplinary action has kept me from a night’s rest for some time. I pored over the literature on Angels and couldn’t find anything to corroborate his theories. However, something I’ve read before caught my attention.

In the 6th passage of chapter 43 on Sergio’s Metaphysics of Being, something stuck out to me given the context of the scribe’s claims.

“Those who stood by the Divine maintained their formless purity and those who did not, crystallized into form.

The nature of the heavens could not allow for Finite to taint the perfect Infinite.

So those who abdicated their connection to Divinity fled to a lower form.”

Consensus holds that this passage refers specifically to man’s progenitors, but what if it wasn’t speaking of us?

source_en:
Siron, excuse my apparent lack of enthusiasm for our esteemed philanthropist at the gathering last evening.

Mathias better know what he’s doing involving that mogul from Nachtendale in Lunitarian affairs. The Holy Lineage entrusted the Archspire to not only study the ‘Artifacts’ but also keep them away from prying eyes.

However, I must concede that the arcanists have made tremendous progress relative to our stagnancy over the last century, and pressure from The Holy Lineage to see results has been mounting.

The mogul assures us that his work will yield promising results, and the Archspire will take full credit for what is to come. A deal too good to be true, if you ask me. I hope to be pleasantly surprised.

I implore you to heed my warnings about these heretics. No longer can we stand idly while these “Reborn” further lead your flock astray. Faithfully yours, S M

Like myself, the Akyrians who occupy these halls show a callous disregard for human life, but something interesting occurred when the initiates brought me another prisoner last evening. It was a devout man from the Archspire, one of the faith’s most loyal Solomon couldn’t seduce. I had little intention of infecting him; he’d sooner make finer biomass for the flora. Then came “the jailer,” one of the first to cross into our realm here in Shoreditch. As I requested, he brought me more vials of the growth hormone derived from the Warden. As he turned to leave, he saw the man Lunar Crescent hanging from his neck. Before I could ask that he be left alone, the Jailer shoved his fingers into his eyes and tore his head from his shoulders.

source_en:
The Dry Rot King, his people called it before the name was the last word any of them could still speak.

The Saedrics were his people: keepers of the old groves, who counted their years in harvests rather than kings. When their god began to rot in the dark, something of him reached back through the roots and into them. They did not die. They dried.
Now they are the Rot Kin, and they tend the forest the way grief tends a grave. The stone was never a prison so much as a wound stitched shut. It holds a god, but it does not heal him and it does not silence him. The wardens who guard it report the same thing across centuries,the longer he is kept, the less of E'frae remains, and the more of the rot answers in his place.

Where his influence reaches, the land does not burn or drown. It simply gives up. Leaves brown on a windless day. Timber crumbles though no rain has touched it. Animals lie down and do not rise again. It is not death, exactly, death is an ending, this is a slow forgetting of how to be alive.

My dear Wensleigh,

Two candles, and the second already crooked. You will forgive the haste. I write quickly because this evening, when it comes, will be very long.

You are a rare student. I do not say this to flatter you. I say it because the saying has become rare. Most who pass through my hall admire the lantern, and the pleasing circle of light it permits them. You have always been of a different garden, most content at the edges of the light.

I will speak briefly tonight. The Cardinal will speak longer. Our Patron will speak last, and the wine will be very fine, and you will be bored, and that is right and good.

After the toasts — when the older guests find the air heavy and retire to their carriages — find me. There is a smaller gathering for the few who have taken the trouble to look further. I have argued for your inclusion. The argument was not difficult. It rarely is, with you.

Wear something you can move in. Pin nothing to your collar that you would mourn.

Yours, in faith and in the better light to come,
 F.

source_en:
Asher,

The bolt on my study door is a brass thing of poor manufacture, three-pin tumbler, replaced in the autumn of '02 by Greaves, who did the work for a guinea and complained the entire afternoon. I mention it because tonight I am grateful for it, which is more consideration than the bolt has ever earned.

Three chairs at the Fellow's Council are empty now. Marvenne. Hollis. Old Korbel.

Marvenne told me last spring she had had words with Master Felwyl over his revised Eveirington reading list. He was, she said, unwilling to entertain disagreement. Two months later — sabbatical. The other two had complaints in similar weather, and now the registry tells me they are abroad.

Marvenne has no family abroad.

One other thing, and you may laugh. I have served at Elk Grove forty-one years. I know how the chapel candles burn. They have been burning low. Low when no one is in the hall. Low when the windows are shut.

I am not imagining it.

I will see you at the Gala. Do not approach me first. I will find you near the orchestra, between the second movement and the third, when no one is listening because everyone is listening.

Yours,
 H.

source_en:
Tuesday. Botanical Studies, third hour. Eight of us, two missing — Wynn says it's the cough going around, but I never met anyone who liked Wynn enough to tell her where they actually were.

Master Felwyl brought a new specimen today. He carried it himself, which he never does. A small thing in a glass dome. Pale pink, with red veins. He said the name in old Lunitarian and I didn't catch it. I'll ask Cora. Cora always remembers.

He let us each look. Up close it pulses, very softly, like it is breathing. Master Felwyl said this was not breathing. He said it was simply sap. He smiled when he said it.

It is a little ugly. The stem is too white. But the flower is, I must admit, the loveliest thing I have ever seen. When I smelled it, my mouth watered, which is silly. I keep thinking about it. I keep thinking about it the way I would think about a boy.

Then the bell, and we filed out, and I forgot to copy the diagram from the board.

Oh — the Gala is on the Eve. Father bought me a sash. I look very serious in it. He laughed. I was offended, then I laughed.

I'll write of the party after.

Monday. Fitting at Madame Auvern's at the Sixth Bell. Tea at Reverence Hall. The Devereaux woman is wearing crimson, of course she is, the woman has the imagination of a banker's wife. Sash for me, then; one cannot match.

Tuesday. The Cathedral Auxiliary, then dinner at the Haedriks. Edmund pleads his nerves and will not come. He has pled his nerves three weeks running. I am beginning to suspect his nerves know of nothing other than pleading.

Wednesday. Sat for my portrait. The painter remarked that the moon has been very red of late, and asked if I had noticed. I said the moon is not noticed if one is properly dressed.

Thursday. Lunch with Vivienne. She said two of her staff have given notice without explanation. I gave her mine. I have a girl from Pontoon Town who is grateful and quiet and has not yet had the chance to learn how to leave.

Friday. Confession. I lied about the usual things. Father Olm seemed distracted. I asked after his health. He said he had been sleeping poorly, and that the chapel candles were burning low.

The Eve. The Spire. Crimson sash. Eighth Bell. Carriage at the door.

I am told one must, on these occasions, smile.

Halvern Room, half past the Tenth Bell. Knock twice, then once. Five of them — Devereaux, Halhurst, Old Pellaby, Tannig, Anderson.

Be brief. Be brief. Be brief.

Open with the joke about Halhurst's clocks. Clocks paid by the hour. Wait for the laugh. If they do not laugh, turn serious abruptly.

Then: the Church is exhausted... Sold its last seat three hundred years ago... No new pews... Nothing it could offer me would be enough even if it still had something to offer.

Then: Mr. Moore is the only ledger in the city large enough to carry what is coming. Not flattery. "This is merely Mathematics."

Then: buy in now, or be bought later. The wise man does not need this said twice. (say this out loud so they think of themselves wise)

The Veil... PAUSE HERE... The Veil is a wall between two rooms. One side has stopped paying its rent. The other side has been keeping the books for a thousand years. The rent is owed. The reopening is not a question. It is a date.

Tell them: my name is on the contract.

Tell them: I am not selling. I am inviting.

On Halhurst's daughter — only speak of her if he raises her name first. Then: She is well thought of by Master Felwyl. Let it sit.

Close. Slowly. We are not buyers. We are founders. We are the seed of the next House.

Smile. They will think it modesty.
— B. C.

source_en:
Shipments from the herbary have ceased completely now, so I’ve not been able to properly mix my tinctures. 

I’ve had to dilute what supplies I have down to the point of imagination.  It’s just as well then that so much of the city has fled. 

I had only one patient come in yesterday for her weekly powders. Usually, it's half-ash, half-desiccated bone broth that's prescribed for a touch of the dropsy, but now it's ash alone I have to serve. 

Whether her constitution can tell the difference, I don't suppose I'm like to ever know.  

Today, no one has come in at all.

It’s only the brave who stayed. And the foolish.  

Since my own tincture for bravery—good mead—has long run out, I guess I know which I am. 

I’ve nothing to share now but wishes and water. 

But then, maybe that’s all I ever had.

Forgive me. I hope you live to see this, but I could not wait. 

If you are reading this, brother, do not go home. The inquisition has both our names, though from whom I couldn't guess.  It might have been anyone, but it doesn't matter now. Anynmore than the truth matters.  

So go West. Follow the river out, and head for the woods. Rember that place where grandfather took us hunting as children?  

You got your first rabbit there, if I remember. A better shot than me, even then.

I pray I will see you again. If not in this life, then in the hereafter. 

If I don’t make it, and you do, then know this about my last moments. I will try to take one of the bastards with me.  

-Your brother

What's reborn can be rekilled. Remember that, you fools. 

It's the cult that brought this down on all of us. I'd wager anything.

It was only me that ran. 

It’s important I write that here, so it’s recorded. I’d want no stench of desertion to be levied against the others, who fought bravely to a man. 

Their names should be clean, unlike mine—Daerun Bogmire, as it’s recorded in the sentry lists. A name, even bad as it is, that I couldn't live up to. 

Or maybe I did live up to it.  To run is in my name.

What does heaven look like, I wonder? Or mayhap it’s hell I should be thinking on. 

Soon I’ll know. The cut is deep, but that’s not what I’m afraid of. It’s the bite. The bite worries me. This bite that gives me frenzied thoughts. 

It’s not too long now afore I go. I feel it rising, like a fever. Please forgive me.     

I seen the walking bones. I knew them when they held flesh. Good men, some of them. Bad men, others. But as bones they are made equal as never they were in life. They are the damned. As soon am I.  

Or am already. 

Goodbye. 

The Bogmire name dies with me.  Good riddance.

أنا الوحيد الذي هرب. 

من المهم أن أكتب ذلك هنا، لكي يُسجل. لا أريد أن تُنسب رائحة الفرار إلى الآخرين، الذين قاتلوا بشجاعة حتى الرمق الأخير.

أو ربما كنت جديراً به بالفعل. فالهرب هو ما يحمله اسمي.

أتساءل، كيف يبدو الجنة؟ أو ربما يجب أن أفكر في الجحيم. 

قريباً سأعرف. الجرح عميق، لكن ليس هذا ما أخشاه. إنها العضة. العضة هي ما يقلقني. هذه العضة التي تمنحني أفكاراً محمومة. 

لن يتبقى الكثير قبل أن أرحل. أشعر بها تتصاعد، مثل الحمى. أرجوكم سامحوني. 

رأيت العظام السائرة. عرفتهم حين كانت تحمل اللحم. رجال صالحون، بعضهم. ورجال سيئون، آخرون. لكن كعظام، أصبحوا متساوين كما لم يكونوا أبداً في حياتهم. إنهم الملعونون. وسأكون كذلك قريباً. 

أو ربما أنا ملعون بالفعل. 

وداعاً. 

اسم بوغماير يموت معي. فلتذهب الجحيم.

Another test subject was martyred today in pursuit of knowledge. We managed to keep his soul bound to flesh for nearly a fortnight after his heart stopped beating. 

Just before he expired the second time, he looked up at me and spoke my mother’s name. 

He could not possibly have known it, of course. 

At least not before he died the first time. 

He told me that my mother knew what I’d done. That she’d whispered to him that she was ashamed. 

I told him my mother had been dead these many years, and asked where he'd heard the whispers.  

He only smiled and said, "Not in Divine's Throne Room, that's for certain."

Your Eminence, I pray we are not too late. I don’t understand the church’s slow response to this threat. The Cult of the Reborn grows and grows, like a noxious and dangerous weed in the beautiful garden of our city, yet we do nothing!

They call us toothless old fools as they incite heresy in the street. 

Why does the church not react? The influence of this cult increases by the day. There have been murders, kidnappings, and even rumors of heretical experimentations. Stories of abominations have reached my ears.  

There is a sickness spreading through the world, and this cult is at the heart of it.

The enemy is not just at our doorstep, but also seated at our very tables. The Lunitarian Church must take action before the wound grows too great. Please, I implore you.  

Ever your faithful servant,

-Father Ortney
